care.title: Deck lifespan and long-term care
care.intro: Composite decking can provide decades of outdoor use. How long your deck lasts depends on the boards you choose, the structure beneath them, installation and ongoing care.

items.title: Framing and installation
items.body: The deck boards are only part of the structure. Joists, beams, posts and connections need to remain sound throughout its use. When replacing an older deck surface, have the existing framing assessed before deciding what can stay. Board spacing, support and fasteners should follow the requirements for the selected decking.

items.title: Moisture and drainage
items.body: Rain, snow and trapped debris can affect the deck and its supporting structure. Keep spaces between boards clear and address areas where water collects. Pay attention to the connection between the deck and the house, along with the condition of the framing below.

items.title: Sun exposure and everyday wear
items.body: Sunlight, foot traffic, pets and moving furniture affect how the surface looks over time. Consider how you use the space when comparing colors and finishes, and follow the manufacturer’s guidance for protecting the boards.

items.title: Cleaning and upkeep
items.body: Remove leaves and debris, clean spills promptly and use the cleaning methods recommended for your decking collection. Trex Transcend Lineage can be cleaned with soap and water; follow Trex’s care guide for specific stains and approved cleaning tools.

care.footnote: Manufacturer warranty coverage is separate from expected service life. Review the terms for the exact decking collection you select.
